steps.title: Welcome
steps.body: A short setup to get this app ready. Nothing here is required; you can close it and come back later.

steps.title: Demo data (optional)
steps.body: Load a small example dataset so the lists, detail pages and dashboards show a working product straight away. The data is obviously sample data, it is safe to run more than once, and it can be removed afterwards. Skip this on a production install.

store._note: Configuration exchange, not rows. There is deliberately NO `installable` allowlist: a set exists to introduce schemas the instance does not have YET, so listing schemas planninq already owns would refuse exactly the sets worth installing. ⚠️ An EMPTY `installable` means install NOTHING, not install anything.

pages.title: Store

config.title: Store
config.description: Install planning configurations that other organisations have published: a project template, a set of stages, or the flows behind them.

pages._note: ADR-114 Decision 4 / ADR-080. Declarative: openregister hosts the store plane, so this app writes NO store controller. With no registry configured the page renders the app's built-in items and makes NO network call.

widgets.title: My projects
widgets._note: The two non-KPI panels (My projects, Quick actions), rendered by the `project-panels` widget type, which src/registry.js maps to DashboardPanels. CnWidgetGrid resolves a manifest widget by its TYPE against the app registry before the library catalog, so the key there is the type string, not this id. DashboardPanels is a plain component, NOT a nested CnDashboardPage: hydra gate-15 rejects a dashboard inside a dashboard.

pages._note: Project index rendered as cards with a client-side status chip filter over filteredProjects, plus a free-text field. The chip row is a filter surface CnIndexPage does not express, so the list is a host-app SFC.
pages.title: Projects

pages._note: Bespoke Kanban board: one column per project status, with drag-to-transition between columns and a per-card move menu listing the other columns as targets. No v2 primitive renders a column-per-status board or owns the drop-to-transition write.
pages.title: Project board

pages._note: Backlog under a project: a parent breadcrumb back to the board above an ordered task list scoped to :id. The parent-scoped header is the part CnIndexPage does not carry.
pages.title: Backlog

pages._note: Gantt over a project's tasks: positioned bars plus dependency arrows drawn between them, fed by /api/timeline. The roadmap type renders milestones on a track and has no vocabulary for task bars with dependency edges.
pages.title: Timeline

pages._note: Task detail that combines a CnObjectSidebar with an inline time-entry log written against the same task. A detail page renders the record; the embedded logging surface is what makes this custom.
pages.title: Task

pages._note: Week timesheet: entries grouped per day with inline edit and a project selector. A grouped, editable grid over time entries, which no v2 list primitive expresses.
pages.title: Timesheet

pages._note: Board picker: the projects a user can open a board for, as entry points rather than records. The cards route to /projects/:id and expose no record actions.
pages.title: Boards

pages._note: Capacity across projects: one row per assignee aggregating allocation over the projects they appear in. An aggregate view with no single backing record, so it is neither an index nor a dashboard of widgets.
pages.title: Portfolio

pages._note: ADR-112 / ADR-114 Decision 3. Portfolio already existed and moves here from the main navigation. The other two are new, and are declarative type:dashboard pages over the app's own register — no per-app component and no per-app controller, the same reasoning that put the Store in openregister.

pages._note: Declarative. Every filter here is scalar equality, which is the only kind OpenRegister's aggregation endpoint can evaluate: a multi-value or relative-date filter is accepted and then silently not applied, which is how decidiq's KPI cards came to show wrong numbers.

Features & roadmap
pages._note: ADR-018 / ADR-114 Decision 5. Rendered by the shared CnFeaturesAndRoadmapView, which reads the committed docs/features.json and OpenRegister's GitHub proxy. No per-app customisation of the view itself.

pages.title: Flows
pages._note: ADR-110 Decision 4: a planninq flow operates on projects and tasks, so the authoring surface belongs here rather than behind a link to another app's list. type:"index" over the NAMED flows source, which is the canonical shape: a flow lives in OpenRegister's native flow store, not a register/schema pair, so the object-backed index cannot address it. nextcloud-vue marks the dedicated `flows` page type deprecated. rowRoute names FlowDetail by route NAME, without which the row click falls back to the source's own /flows path.

pages.title: Flow
pages._note: The shared CnFlowDetail canvas over the same single engine (ADR-065), scoped to this app.

observability._note: AppHost manifest (ADR-040). The observability block reproduces the output of the now-deleted hand-written HealthController + MetricsController; /api/health and /api/metrics are aliased to AppHost\Controller\GenericHealth#index / GenericMetrics#index in appinfo/routes.php. The deepLinks block replaces the hand-written DeepLinkRegistrationListener, read at event time by the generic listener. Parity: the database health check and the implicit {appId}_info/{appId}_up metrics match the pre-adoption contract — those two are derived from the runtime app id, so they read planninq_info/planninq_up after the planix -> planninq rename; the task/project object counts are a documented intentional improvement (object-count observability the bespoke MetricsController never emitted). The `register` and `registerSlug` values below are the OpenRegister register slug, not the app id — they moved from `planix` to `planninq` alongside the MigrateRegisterSlug repair step that renames the register ROW. They only work because that step runs: the slug is what a lookup resolves a register by, so a renamed slug here without the row rename would resolve nothing (and, on the import path, fork a second empty register). This was an observability-only manifest until 2026-08-31, when planninq adopted the manifest shell: it now also carries `dependencies`, `menu` and `pages`, CnAppRoot renders the nav and the OpenRegister dependency gate, and vue-router routes are built from `pages[]` in main.js. The former top-level appId/name keys were removed 2026-07-06 (not part of the v2 contract; the app id comes from the runtime).
